sources.title: Budgeted multi-agent writing with a deterministic controller
sources.snippet: A bounded, reference-passing controller kept prompt growth linear in the number of iterations while reported quality kept improving across eleven drafts.

sources.title: Token-aware scheduling for long-running language-model pipelines
sources.venue: Proceedings of the 2023 Conference on Systems for Machine Learning
sources.snippet: Scheduling on token estimates rather than wall time held tail latency flat as the number of pipeline stages grew, at a small cost in throughput.

texts.text: Agentic writing systems rarely report what their iterations cost, so a quality gain is hard to separate from brute force. Nguyen and Alvarez (2024) describe a controller that passes references instead of full text between agents, which keeps prompt size tied to the number of sections rather than to the length of the draft [[CITE:01ARZ3NDEKTSV4RRFFQ69G5FC2]]. Petrova (2023) reports the same effect in scheduling, where token-aware admission kept tail latency flat as the pipeline grew [[CITE:01ARZ3NDEKTSV4RRFFQ69G5FD3]]. This article asks whether that discipline survives when five specialised agents share one append-only ledger. The pilot run in the brief suggests it does: eleven iterations produced a measurable quality gain while total spend stayed inside a single run budget. The contribution is a controller design that makes the trade visible, and a first measurement.
